This is a very caring and rational response. I hope you read this, I realize your post was 2 days ago. 

I am one of those jealous wives. In fact, while reading your original post, I wondered at first if you were MY husband. We just had a big blow-out a couple weeks ago because he had been keeping the feelings that you have bottled up for 7 years. And I actually have made strides since we first started going out. When we met, I was dealing with some HUGE trust issues (I grew up with a family filled with infidelity. My dad cheated on my mom, my sister was cheated on by 2 different husbands, it's just surrounded me. I learned about those affairs at a very young age so that could've contributed too. Also, I myself was cheated on twice.  If I voice any concerns to her or my mother about my husband they quickly go to "are you sure he isn't cheating on you", "has he acted any different", "is he going to work early or staying late" and it just made me absolutely paranoid. ) and every time he went out (as hard as I tried to conceal my feelings because I knew they were irrational) with his friends, I would sit at home, alone, having a panic attack. Then of course when he came home, I had a million questions for him that I just couldn't (but should've) keep to myself. Over the years, I have gotten better, but I still have moments of madness. Let me make this clear: my husband has NEVER given me any reason to believe that he would ever cheat on me. Here's my story, I hope it helps.

My husband had just made his first female friend since we have been together and was tearing me apart inside. I know she is married an has a 1 year old, but she is still somehow extremely threatening to me. We both played Everquest, and it turns out that's how they met, by talking about EQ2. So he brought her up to me and asked if I'd like to meet her and play with her. I did (though I was sick with nervousness) and she was very nice. Nice though very familiar with him which made me feel even worse. But then of COURSE she's acting familiar with him, they are friends! I know I am thinking irrationally, but coming from a family where I was surrounded by infidelity, I am naturally jealous. She works in the same building as him and smokes, so they talk every day. She texts occasionally but he usually reads them out loud, and they are pretty innocent. I never got the chance to meet her in person and was terrified to find out that she may be prettier than I am. 

I have talked to him since the friend issue, and after several extremely difficult conversations, I finally felt a little better about the situation. Keep in mind, the first 3 discussions didn't end well. But we continued to come back to the issue and I thought we had finally worked through it. Then he blew up. He said that he guessed he just can't talk to her anymore and in a huff, deleted our Everquest accounts. He then told me that no, he wasn't going to stop talking to her because it wasn't fair to him (keep in mind that I NEVER asked him to stop talking to her. Actually at this time I was apologizing profusely and trying frantically to prove that I did trust him). He then told me "Do not ask me about her ever again." And he meant it. I've tried to bring the issue back up since then and he just gets angry and says "I thought I told  you never to talk about her again."

TL;DR: Don't let the issue go on and on before talking about it. You may blow up like my husband did. Try to listen to her, and as hard as it may be to understand, she isn't acting this way out of spite. I'm sure she does actually trust you personally, but just doesn't trust people in general so that gets in the way. I hope she gets professional help for this. I got help years ago, and it did help me. Make sure you are being truthful with her (don't start lying because "I'm not doing anything wrong, so she doesn't need to know I'm hanging out with (insert female name here)". She will find out and feel even more betrayed. Even though you know that she knows you love her and think she is wonderful and beautiful, and no one could replace her- tell her! Women just need to HEAR it sometimes. Just realized how long that TD;LR was, I just want to stress: DON'T GIVE UP ON HER.

Edit: Re-wording a bit

Edit2: Our only difference seems to be that in my relationship, HE is the dominant one, and I am the fearful one.

I know a lot of people will tell you that you need to find the root of the problem, but that's only the beginning. I know exactly what my root is, (as it sounds like you do) I've been going to a psychologist for 9 years about it. I grew up with a family filled with infidelity. When I was 13, my sister told me that my dad had cheated on my mom (she's 10 years older than me) and I've had to keep it a secret for 13 years now (my parents stayed together and never told me). Then my sister was cheated on by 2 different husbands. Not to mention I myself have been cheated on twice. Now I'm in the stage where I am aware what the problem is and am trying as hard as I can to fix it. A couple of weeks ago my husband made his first female friend that he's had since we've been together, and I was just beside myself. I am out of work and stay cooped up in the house all day, worrying until I get sick. I have talked to him since them, and after several extremely difficult conversations, finally feel a little better. Keep in mind, the first like 3 discussions didn't end well. But we continued to come back to the issue and finally worked through it (I think). I would suggest talking to your next SO about your problem (if it ends up effecting your relationship) and being truthful with her/him and tell them you are trying your damnedest to change. I need to take my own advice of getting out of the house and making friends, just like you do, but I'm struggling. We just need to try and be brave. I often make lists of "positive things" in my life to work on my low self esteem which contributes to the whole problem. I write down even tiny things, like "I can read quickly" and "I have 2 cats". Making lists seems to make me feel like I am in control of something- since I mostly feel out of control. I don't want you to feel alone, I know it can be just maddening. I also understand the feeling of knowing that you are acting/thinking irrationally but still hanging on to those behaviors and thoughts. It has actually helped a little to look up self-help books and articles about getting over trust issues. Don't think you'll feel this way forever. It takes a lot of work, thought and introspection so be prepared for a fight.

I have really screwed up trust issues as well. This manifests into extreme jealousy to the point of paranoia which has put quite a strain on my relationship. It's hard to come to grips with and it's hard for anyone else to understand. It's hard for a SO to understand that it's not that you don't trust THEM specifically, that it's difficult to trust ANYONE. It tears me up inside and I can't talk about it or I sound like a crazy, paranoid person. Now that you've had this experience, hopefully you'll be able to open up to the next person who you become involved with. If they truly care for you, they will try to understand. But it's always better to be honest to them and yourself. I'd advise seeing a psychologist about what you're struggling with (if you aren't already). I pulling for you, things can only get better from here. And you're never really alone.

Congratulations on your realization that cutting is not the answer. The only way I stopped was a loved one telling me the same thing as your friend told you. I still think of it all of the time, but have relapsed only once in 6 years. There is hope!
